transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-23
Time: 11:00 AM PT / 19:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Mike (MaplePoint - Head Sec), Aisha (CTO), Derek (Platform)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on security posture and which hosting mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private) fits MaplePoint's fintech constraints. Main concerns: SOC2/ISO attestation, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC granularity, audit log retention/export, encryption and KMS/HSM options, and data deletion/retention policies.

Topics covered:
- Compliance artifacts (SOC2 Type II, ISO27001)
- SSO (SAML/SCIM) and provisioning
- RBAC roles and least-privilege model
- Audit logs: retention, export, tamper-proofing
- Encryption: at-rest, KMS integration, HSM support
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs (latency, cost, data residency)
- Next steps: send docs, schedule HSM deep-dive, share retention matrix

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do quick intros. I'm Samir, AE for Redwood Inference.
[00:00:08] Mike: Hi, Mike here, head of security at MaplePoint. Thanks.
[00:00:11] Aisha: Aisha, CTO. We're trying to understand the security surface — especially how you handle keys, logs, and SAML.
[00:00:20] Lena: Great, I'll cover technical bits — our KMS integrations, RBAC, and audit logging. Quick note, if things get deep we'll book a follow-up with our infra security architect.
[00:00:32] Samir: High level first — MaplePoint is a fintech, so I assume you have PII and payment-related data?
[00:00:38] Mike: Yes, we handle transaction metadata and user PII, though we try to avoid storing full payment tokens. We need control over retention and the ability to show auditors logs.
[00:00:47] Derek: Also performance — we run low-latency customer flows, so we're trying not to trade off too much latency for security.
[00:00:55] Lena: Understood. For context, Redwood offers three hosting modes: Hosted API (fastest onboarding), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC / on-prem). Each mode has different options for key mgmt and network isolation.
[00:01:10] Mike: Can you spell out KMS options? We want customer-managed keys.
[00:01:14] Lena: Sure. For Hosted we support cloud KMS integrations — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault — where you can bring your key. For Dedicated we can support customer-managed KMS with VPC peering and option to use an HSM-backed key via your cloud provider. For Private deployments we can wire to your on-prem HSM or HSM appliance. There's also an option for envelope encryption so model weights/artefacts are encrypted with a root key you control.
[00:01:40] Aisha: Envelope encryption, okay. Is the KV cache encrypted separately or under the same key?
[00:01:44] Lena: The KV/prefix cache is treated as ephemeral in memory but when persisted for cache warm-up it's encrypted at rest using the deployment's data key; that key is managed via the KMS setup you choose. Note: some of our docs call it "KV cache" others will say "key-value cache" — apologies for the naming noise in the docs.
[00:02:05] Mike: How about HSM — do you support PKCS11 or Cloud HSM?
[00:02:09] Lena: We support CloudHSM providers — e.g., AWS CloudHSM — and can integrate via PKCS11 in Private installs. For Hosted there's an integration pattern where you control the CMK and we call it for envelope operations but HSM-level key material never leaves your HSM. We'll need a technical deep-dive to map specifics.
[00:02:28] Samir: Mike, are you required to have FIPS/HSM level attestations?
[00:02:31] Mike: We don't have a hard FIPS requirement yet, but our auditors prefer HSM-backed key control for production.
[00:02:37] Derek: On RBAC — what granularity do you offer? We need per-team access and token scoping.
[00:02:42] Lena: Redwood has route-level and token-level RBAC. You can create roles like "model-deploy", "billing-read", "audit-reader". Tokens are scoped to routes/models and you can set expiration. For Dedicated and Private, RBAC can integrate with your SSO provider for group-based roles through SCIM.
[00:03:02] Aisha: SCIM is important — we want automated provisioning and deprovisioning from Okta.
[00:03:07] Lena: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user and group provisioning. There's sometimes small mapping work depending on your IdP where we map groups to roles.
[00:03:16] Mike: Audit logs — retention and tamper-proofing? Our compliance requires 7 years retention for some events and an immutable audit trail.
[00:03:24] Lena: By default, hosted retains detailed request logs for 90 days. For Dedicated and Private, you control the log sink. You can ship logs to your GCS/AWS bucket and apply immutability policies there. We also support pushing audit events to your SIEM (e.g., Splunk) in near-real time. For tamper-proofing, we support write-once buckets and can sign logs with a key you control.
[00:03:48] Mike: So exportable logs — we can keep them externally with retention policies. Good. Is there an API to pull logs for auditors?
[00:03:55] Lena: Yes, we provide an audit log export API and also support S3/GCS export. For Hosted customers who need longer retention we have an add-on for extended log retention and archival.
[00:04:05] Derek: On data deletion, if a user asks for deletion, how quickly can you purge their data?
[00:04:10] Lena: We have a deletion pipeline for customer data — depending on where data is stored (cache, logs, model telemetry) deletion can be immediate for cached/persistent stores and we can scavenge logs per your retention window. For Hosted we can coordinate to delete developer data within an SLA; for Private you control the deletion process. We'll need to confirm exact SLAs in the follow-up.
[00:04:30] Mike: What about model telemetry — do you retain prompts/outputs for quality monitoring?
[00:04:34] Samir: We do collect telemetry by default for platform health and quality — it's on by default but can be disabled. We also offer a privacy mode where sensitive fields are redacted client-side with SDK helpers.
[00:04:44] Aisha: Are there contractual controls for disabling telemetry?
[00:04:47] Samir: Yes, in Dedicated/Private mode you can disable telemetry or restrict the retention period via contract and config.
[00:04:53] Lena: Also worth noting: when you request Dedicated capacity, you get isolated GPU pools and an SLA; network egress and data residency can be restricted to your region. Private gives the most control but longer lead time.
[00:05:05] Mike: About SOC2 and ISO docs — do you have attestation and scope detail? The auditors will ask for system boundaries.
[00:05:10] Samir: Yes, we'll send SOC2 Type II report and an ISO27001 summary with system scoping notes. We'll highlight what is in-scope for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[00:05:19] Mike: Is the SOC2 covering the management plane or only the control plane? We need clarity where customer data sits vs the control plane.
[00:05:25] Lena: Good question. The SOC2 report covers Redwood's control plane operations and our managed infrastructure for Hosted. For Dedicated we have a narrower scope for the shared infra and we can provide the hosting controls; for Private the system boundary shifts significantly to your environment. We'll annotate the report with notes specific to data-in-rest and egress.
[00:05:44] Derek: Encryption at rest — are database backups encrypted too?
[00:05:47] Lena: Backups are encrypted using the same key management approach; if you bring your key, backups are encrypted under your CMK. For extra reassurance we can describe snapshot lifecycle and key rotation policy.
[00:05:58] Mike: Key rotation — how is rotation handled with minimal downtime?
[00:06:01] Lena: We use envelope encryption so rotating the data key is non-disruptive; we roll the KMS CMK and rewrap keys without needing to re-encrypt all blobs. We'll share a rotation doc.
[00:06:11] Aisha: On SSO, what's the typical mapping lag for deprovisioning? We can't have former employees able to call inference.
[00:06:17] Lena: With SCIM provisioning, deprovisioning is immediate once your IdP sends the deprovision event. For token sessions, tokens expire based on TTL; we recommend short TTLs for high-risk roles and immediate revocation via the admin console.
[00:06:31] Samir: Any other constraints on your side we should know about?
[00:06:34] Mike: Network — we need private peering, ideally; no public internet egress for inference traffic in prod.
[00:06:40] Lena: We can do VPC peering for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we offer a private egress option via customer-managed NAT; this requires additional networking setup.
[00:06:51] Derek: How about telemetry sampling rates? We don't want full prompts logged.
[00:06:55] Lena: You can configure sampling rates and enable client-side redaction; we also support PII scrubbing rules in the pipeline.
[00:07:03] Mike: Auditors will ask for proof of immutability for certain logs — can you support append-only logs and signed digests?
[00:07:09] Lena: Yes, for Dedicated/Private we can configure append-only storage and generate signed digests (SHA-based) that can be verified. We'll include an architecture note in the follow-up.
[00:07:22] Samir: Sounds like main asks: SOC2/ISO docs, KMS/HSM options, log export/immutability, SSO/SCIM mapping and deprovisioning timelines, RBAC roles examples, and data retention matrix. We'll get those to you.
[00:07:34] Mike: One last — pricing impact. Does Dedicated with customer-managed KMS/HSM add material cost?
[00:07:40] Samir: There is an uplift for Dedicated + private networking; using cloud HSM also carries cloud provider fees. We'll include a cost estimate in the follow-up.
[00:07:50] Aisha: OK thanks — let's lock a follow-up deep-dive for the KMS/HSM and network team next week if possible.
[00:07:57] Lena: I'll send calendar invites for a technical session and include our infra security architect.
[00:08:01] Samir: Recap and next steps: I'll send SOC2 + ISO docs and security page, Lena will prep KMS/HSM integration notes and the architecture diagram, Mike will share retention/ classification table.
[00:08:12] Mike: Great, expecting docs.
[00:08:15] Aisha: Thanks all.
[00:08:18] Samir: Thanks, we'll follow up.
